title: Service terminated unexpectedly and is being restarted
explanation: A Windows service crashed. The Service Control Manager has a recovery action configured and is automatically restarting it.
commonCauses: Unhandled exception in the service binary
Missing or corrupted dependency (DLL, driver, or config file)
Resource exhaustion (memory or handle leak) in the service process
recommendedAction: Check the service's own event source for the underlying exception; run 'sc qc <service>' to confirm binary path and dependencies.

title: Service terminated unexpectedly (no automatic recovery configured)
explanation: A Windows service crashed and, unlike 7031, has no recovery action configured, so it will remain stopped until manually restarted or the machine reboots.
commonCauses: Unhandled exception in the service binary
A dependent service or driver failed to load
recommendedAction: Restart the service manually after investigating the root cause, then configure a recovery policy with 'sc failure'.

title: Failed logon attempt
explanation: An account failed to log on. A single occurrence is often just a mistyped password; a burst of these in a short window can indicate brute-force activity or a stale credential in a scheduled task or service.
commonCauses: User mistyped their password
A scheduled task or service is using an expired/rotated credential
Brute-force or password-spray attempt against the account
recommendedAction: Check the Logon Type and source workstation/IP in the event detail. If unexplained and repeated, treat the account as potentially targeted.

title: System rebooted without a clean shutdown
explanation: The system restarted without first shutting down cleanly. This usually points to a power loss, a hard hang, or a hardware fault rather than a normal user-initiated restart.
commonCauses: Power failure or the machine was hard-reset
A kernel-level driver crash (bugcheck) that didn't produce a visible bluescreen log
Overheating-triggered hardware shutdown
recommendedAction: Correlate with EventID 1001 (BugCheck) and 6008 around the same timestamp; check PSU/thermal health if this repeats.

title: Previous system shutdown was unexpected
explanation: Logged the first time the Event Log service starts after a shutdown that wasn't clean (no matching orderly-shutdown event was recorded).
commonCauses: Power loss
User held the power button
System crash/hang requiring a hard reset
recommendedAction: Pair with EventID 41 for kernel-level context on the same incident.

title: File system corruption detected on a volume
explanation: NTFS detected internal structure corruption on a volume. This can be caused by unexpected power loss during a write, failing storage hardware, or (rarely) tampering.
commonCauses: Unclean shutdown mid-write
Failing disk sectors
Faulty storage controller or cabling
recommendedAction: Run 'chkdsk <volume> /scan' (read-only) first; check S.M.A.R.T. status before attempting a repair pass.

title: An error was detected on a device during a paging operation
explanation: The disk driver reported an I/O error during a read/write operation - a common early indicator of a failing physical disk.
commonCauses: Failing or worn-out physical disk
Loose or faulty SATA/NVMe connection
Storage controller driver issue
recommendedAction: Check S.M.A.R.T. attributes immediately; back up data before the drive degrades further.

title: DNS name resolution timed out
explanation: A DNS query for a name did not receive a response within the timeout window from any configured DNS server.
commonCauses: DNS server unreachable or overloaded
Network connectivity issue between the client and DNS server
Misconfigured DNS server address
recommendedAction: Verify configured DNS servers respond via 'Resolve-DnsName', and check network path/firewall rules to them.

title: Group Policy processing was slow, or a network problem occurred
explanation: Group Policy detected slow link processing or a network issue while contacting a domain controller for policy application.
commonCauses: Slow or unreliable link to the domain controller
DNS resolution problems for the domain
Domain controller under heavy load or unreachable
recommendedAction: Run 'gpresult /h report.html' on the affected machine and check DC connectivity/latency.
